entities.name: Vettius Agorius Basilius Mavortius
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Vettius Agorius Basilius Mavortius was a Roman aristocrat of the sixth century who lived under Ostrogothic rule in Italy and held the ordinary consulship in 527. He belonged to the interlinked basilius–Agorius senatorial milieu that preserved classical literary culture—editing and reading pagan Latin poets even as Catholic orthodoxy and Gothic kingship structured politics.

His consulship falls in the reign of Justin I / early Justinian from the eastern vantage, and under Athalaric/Amalasuintha's Ostrogothic regime in Italy—illustrating how western senators still occupied Roman honorific office within a Gothic kingdom soon to face Justinian's reconquest.

Mavortius is often associated with scholarly attention to Horace and other classics, a reminder that late antique Italy's aristocracy remained a carrier of literary tradition on the brink of the Gothic War.
